title: Ruma Bolon (Batak Traditional House)
description: The monumental, ship-like wooden houses of the Batak people built entirely without nails, symbolizing the three realms of the universe.
detailedContent:
Ruma Bolon is the majestic traditional house of the Toba Batak. Characterized by its soaring, saddle-backed boat-shaped roof, the house represents a massive ship navigating the seas of life, designed to withstand earthquakes without a single metal nail.

The house is built on sturdy wooden stilts resting on flat stone foundations, using intricate mortise-and-tenon joints secured by rattan ropes.

Architecturally, Ruma Bolon is divided vertically into three distinct tiers, reflecting the Batak cosmic view:
1. **The Under-house (Bara)**: The dark space beneath the floorboards where livestock was kept. It represents "Banua Toru"—the chaotic underworld of spirits and beasts.
2. **The Living Quarters (Tonga)**: The open, communal main hall where human families cooked, slept, and worked. It represents "Banua Tonga"—the active middle world of humans.
3. **The Attic (Sabu)**: The high, dusty space below the thatched roof where sacred family heirlooms, masks, and seeds were stored. It represents "Banua Ginjand"—the celestial upper world of gods and ancestors.

The facade of Ruma Bolon is heavily decorated with "Gorga"—intricate red, black, and white woodcarvings depicting swirling vines, protective animal eyes, and lizards representing patience and earthbound resilience.
